description: The closed vocabulary of StarCore UI contract v1.1 - see docs/ui-contract.md. The Engine (engine/starcore/ui_contract.py), Mission Control (mission_control/ui/contract.js) and the Android app (mobile/src/satellites/ui/contract.ts) each test that they implement exactly this list. 1.1 only adds to 1.0: every 1.0 document is a valid 1.1 document.

since._note: The minor each block, key or format arrived in. A document that declares an older minor may not use them.

1.2._note: {play: {search}}: the client searches the audio.library provider and plays the results through its media.audio host. {play: {tracks | route, start?, shuffle?, queue?, context?}}: the client plays tracks of the document's own Satellite, which must provide audio.library: tracks binds a list of the page's tracks (or is a list of up to play_tracks bindings to single ones), route is a GET of the Satellite's own route answering {tracks}; the host resolves each id through that provider (never a URL from the document), and refuses when the player plays from another provider. start binds the id of the track to begin with, shuffle shuffles (not with start), queue (next or end) adds to the queue instead (not with start or shuffle), context (text or a binding, at most play_context characters) is reported with each play. Not in a selection (a row's or a tile's quick and menu entries may play). With route, the answer may be paged: {tracks, count, cursor}, tracks the first page, count the whole list's size and cursor the next page's (null at the end); the host asks route with cursor=<cursor> for the next page when about 25 queued tracks are left, and, to shuffle, with positions=<i,j,...> (at most 50 indexes below count) for the tracks at those positions, in that order, drawing positions lazily so a long list is never loaded whole. A document using play requires client media.audio and capability audio.library. {own: section}: the client opens the Satellite's own interface (page.js, native screens) at a section that interface names; a client without one hides the control (a tile skips that entry of its media-grid `open`). {secure: {capability, operation}, item, confirm?, then?}: in a media viewer's or selection's actions, the client runs one of secure_operations on the items, behind its own unlock prompt (never a document form) - see secure_operations. {download: route, name?} and {share: route, name?}: the client fetches the Satellite's own route with its session and saves the file (download) or hands it to the system share sheet (share), named `name`; with `open: true` a download opens the file with the platform instead (a new browser tab, the phone's own viewer). A client that can't (an older Android, a browser that can't share files, a phone without a viewer module) hides the control. Not in a selection or a tile's quick actions. {upload: {multiple}, route, conflict?: {confirm?, route}, then?}: the person picks files on the device and each is sent in turn as the raw body of a POST to route, with $value the file's {name, size} (the name made safe as a download's); a 409 asks conflict.confirm, naming the file, then retries on conflict.route, and declining skips that file; each file is reported, and then (refresh or back) runs once something arrived. A client that can't pick files hides the control. Not in a selection or a tile's quick actions. {section: name}: the client opens the shared document of the Satellite `name` (a binding or a literal) when that Satellite's manifest says it is a section of this one (section_of), and nothing else; a client that can't hides the control. Not in a selection or a tile's quick actions. {sync: {capability}}: the client opens its own sync screen for the document's own Satellite, which must provide that capability (see sync_capabilities); a client without the client capability it needs hides the control. Not in a selection or a tile's quick actions. protected: {capability, setup, forgot?}: the document belongs to a store a client must unlock first - see protected_capabilities. In a protected document only, a route action may declare secrets: {key: {kind, new?}} (kinds in secret_kinds; a new PIN is asked twice): before the request the client asks for each in its own prompt, which names the Satellite asking, and puts it in the body under key - never in $form, $state, storage or logs; and reveal: field: once the request succeeded the client shows that field of the answer once, in its own dialog, until the person confirms they stored it, then forgets it. Neither in a selection or a tile's quick actions, nor with GET. A form field of kind rows has fields (its row's inputs, none of them rows) and an optional add label: the person adds and removes rows, and the form sends them as a list of objects under its key. icons: {name: {fallback, stroke?, paths?}}: the Satellite's own icons, added to the served document by the Engine from its satellite.toml [icons] and icons/ folder (a ui.json may not write it). Any icon key of the document (also through a binding) may name one; a client draws its paths (absolute M, L, C and Z only, in a 24 x 24 box) stroked stroke wide in its own colour, with round caps and joins, and draws the shared fallback when paths is absent. A media-grid with layout row is a shelf: one row that scrolls sideways, without more or selection. A media-list row, like a media-grid tile, may carry quick (up to quick_actions icon actions at its end, each drawn while its visible holds, so a pair with opposite visible bindings is a toggle such as a heart) and menu (up to menu_entries {label, icon?, action, visible?, style?} with the row as $., opened from a More button, a right-click, the context-menu key or Shift+F10 on the web, a More button or a long press on Android; an entry the client can't run, or that needs the server while it is offline, is left out, and an empty menu hides its button). A media-list also takes more (as a list's), item.key (what keeps a row across pages), item.group (headings, as a media-grid's) and item.audio (a binding to a track id of the document's own audio.library provider: the client marks the playing row). then: update, only in a row's or a tile's quick and menu entries, merges the answer's item object into that row and draws it again. {choose: {source, items, item: {title, subtitle?, image?}, title?, empty?, create?: {label, field, route, body?}}, route, body?, conflict?: {confirm?, route, body?}, then?}: the person picks one row of the Satellite's own route `source` (its `items`, drawn as a media-list's rows, with the source row as $. inside item) in a client dialog or sheet, then route runs with that row as $value; create offers one text field, labelled field, and runs its own route with the text as $value instead; a 409 answer asks conflict.confirm (else the answer's error), then runs conflict.route (with conflict.body, else body), and declining runs nothing; cancelling runs nothing. Not in a selection or a tile's quick actions. A media-list with item.key may take reorder: {route, body?}: the person moves a row (by its handle: a drag, Alt+Up or Alt+Down on the web; a drag or Move up and Move down on Android), the list moves at once, and route runs once per move with $value {from, to}, the row's old and new index; a failed move is put back, with the route's error. Not with more or item.group.

secure_operations._note: What the secure action (1.2) may run: a capability, and the operations of it a document may ask for. The client resolves the provider from the catalog, asks for the unlock in its own prompt (a single-use grant for exactly these items), and sends references to the document Satellite's own media.gallery items, built from `item` (a binding to each item's id). Only a Satellite that provides media.gallery may use it, on its own items.

protected_capabilities._note: What a document may name as `protected: {capability, setup, forgot?}` (1.2), and the operations its provider must offer for a client to show it. The provider is the document's own Satellite. Before any page, the client asks status: not configured, no PIN, a security problem or an unreadable PIN opens the `setup` page (a page without params); locked, its own unlock prompt (never a document form), for a full unlock of this session, which offers "Forgot your PIN?" when `forgot` names a page (without params, served without an unlock): that page in place of the prompt, until its way back or its action asks status again. A 403 from any of the document's routes means locked again: the prompt, not an error. The client calls keep while it shows the document, and lock when it closes, is hidden or goes to the background, or the server changes. It keeps nothing: no offline page, no widget, no share action, images and videos never in a disk cache, and on Android the window can't be captured (secure.screen).

sync_capabilities._note: What the sync action (1.2) may open: {sync: {capability}} opens the client's own sync screen for the document's own Satellite, which must provide the capability - {capability: the client capability that screen is}. The document supplies no text, route or setting of the sync: the screen is the client's, and talks to the provider through the capability's operations alone. A client without that client capability hides the control.

operations.list: GET ?path=<absolute path, or empty for the roots> -> {path, parent, entries: [{name, type: dir|file, size, modified}]}; at the roots an entry's name is itself an absolute path

operations.resolve: GET /<id>?quality=&format= -> {track, plan, stream, gain}; stream is a path relative to the provider, answering Range requests

optional_operations.lyrics: GET /<id>?language= -> synced lines or plain text

audio.library._note: Track: {id, title, artist, album, album_id, duration, has_artwork, quality: {label, lossless, hires}}; providers may add keys. See docs/media-audio.md.

operations.list: GET ?kinds=image,video[&limit=N&cursor=C] -> {items: [{id, kind: image|video, title, duration, group}], next}: what a person may pick, newest first; with limit, a page and the cursor of the next (null at the end)

optional_operations.resolve: GET /<id> -> {id, kind}: an item the person may act on now (in the active library); 404 otherwise. What the Engine asks before another Satellite acts on a reference a client sent.
optional_operations.original: GET /<id> -> the stored original of an item in the active library, as a file whose download name is the item's filename; 404 otherwise. Server-side only
optional_operations.release: POST {id, sha256} -> {released: id}: the item leaves the library for good, without a recycle bin and out of every album, because a verified copy now lives elsewhere (a move into a media.vault); 409 when it is no longer in the active library or its original doesn't match sha256. Server-side only
optional_operations.adopt: POST raw body ?name=&modified= -> {id, kind}: takes a file in as an import would (refusing media a media.vault holds) and brings it back from a recycle bin if it was there; 415 for a file the library can't read. Server-side only

media.gallery._note: Picked through the client's media.picker (the pick action). A pick returns references, never paths: [{provider, capability, id, kind}], where provider is the providing Satellite's name. A provider lists only what the signed-in session may see; private or protected media is never listed. original, release and adopt are what a media.vault provider moves media in and out with; they are server-side only: asked by another Satellite through the Engine (starcore.capabilities.call, which sets the request's caller), and a client's request is refused (403).

operations.queue: GET ?device=&expand=1 -> {state: QueueState (+ tracks) | null}; POST {device, state, name, kind} saves it

optional_operations.history: POST {track_id, seconds, device, context} records a play
optional_operations.radio: GET /<track|artist|album|genre>/<id> -> {tracks: [Track]}, to continue when the queue ends
optional_operations.preferences: GET -> preferences; POST {key: value} -> preferences (streaming and download quality, effects, speed)
optional_operations.stream: GET /<id>?quality=&format= -> the audio, answering Range requests; used when resolve can't plan a stream
optional_operations.connect: StarCore Connect under this route: POST register, state, command, transfer; GET devices, events

audio.session._note: A provider's playback session beside its audio.library, from the same Satellite. QueueState: {tracks: [id], order, position, shuffle, repeat, seconds, context}. See docs/media-audio.md.

operations.status: GET -> {configured, pin_set, pin_unreadable, unlocked, expires_at, session_timeout_seconds, idle_seconds, security: {problem}, ...}: whether this session has the store open now, or must unlock first (or set it up). Never extends an unlock
operations.unlock: POST {pin, for?: {operation: "move_in", items: [reference]}} -> with for: {grant, expires_at}, a single-use grant for exactly that move, without unlocking the vault; without: {unlocked, expires_at}, an unlock of this session that ends at session_timeout_seconds or after idle_seconds without a request to the store's routes or to keep. Attempts are counted and locked out as for any unlock
operations.move_in: POST {items: [reference], grant?} -> {moved, failed}: moves media.gallery items into the vault, under this session's unlock or a matching grant; every reference is resolved on the server, again at the moment of the move

optional_operations.keep: POST -> {expires_at}: only for a session that is unlocked (403 otherwise); restarts the idle time, never past session_timeout_seconds. A client calls it while it shows a protected document
optional_operations.biometric: POST challenge {key_id, for?} -> {challenge}; POST unlock {key_id, challenge, signature} -> as unlock, for what the challenge was asked for (a grant with for, a full unlock without). for beside the signature is refused
optional_operations.sealed: GET /<sha256> -> {sealed}: whether media with that digest was moved into the store, so a library refuses to take it back in. Server-side only: the Engine asks every provider, enabled or not (starcore.capabilities.sealed), and a provider that fails counts as yes

media.vault._note: A protected store media can be moved into, by the client's own unlock prompt (the secure action). It offers no way to list or read what it holds: that stays in the providing Satellite's own interface (sealed answers yes or no for one digest, and only to the server). A reference is {provider, capability: "media.gallery", id}, and is only a claim: the server resolves it through the media.gallery provider it knows. A provider moves media in and out with media.gallery's original, release and adopt, through the Engine.

operations.check: GET ?path=<absolute path>[&tree=1] -> {protected, open, message?}: protected when the path is inside an area the provider guards (with tree=1, also a folder that contains one); open when this session may reach it through other Satellites now; message, the provider's words for a refusal

files.protected._note: Server-side only: what the Engine asks before any Satellite serves, lists, indexes, renames or deletes a path on disk (starcore.capabilities.protection). Every provider is asked, enabled or not, and a path is open only when each one says so; a provider that fails or answers anything else keeps the path closed. No client reads it: a provider refuses a request that doesn't come through the Engine.

operations.status: GET ?device= -> {accepts: ["image", "video"], max_bytes, chunk_bytes, device: {name, last_seen, received}}: what the provider takes, and what it holds from this caller; device names it
operations.check: POST {device, items: [{sha256, size}]} (at most 500) -> {known: [sha256], wanted: [sha256]}: known when the provider has it, had it or must not take it again (in the library, in its bin, erased earlier, moved somewhere protected), never saying which; wanted when it would take it; in neither when it is larger than max_bytes
operations.upload: GET /<sha256> -> {offset}: the bytes already held from this caller for that digest. POST /<sha256>?offset=&size=&name=&folder=&taken= with the bytes from offset as an application/octet-stream body of at most chunk_bytes -> {offset}, or once the last byte is in {status: imported|duplicate, id, offset}. Written straight to disk; the whole file's SHA-256 must match (422 otherwise, and it starts again from 0); a wrong offset answers 409 with the right one

optional_operations.devices: GET -> {devices: [{name, last_seen, received, current}]}: the devices that sync, for a status page; refused to a device credential

media.sync._note: One-way backup from a device: a client hashes its media, asks check, and sends only what is wanted, in chunks it can resume after any cut. A provider limits the size, a caller's unfinished uploads (the oldest goes beyond 4) and their age (7 days). Known means safe with the provider: a provider that can't tell (a protected store did not answer) answers 503 to check and upload, never known, and a client concludes nothing from an answer that is not the operation's own. device_credentials: a full session may ask the Engine for a device credential limited to this capability (POST /api/auth/devices), which reaches only the provider's routes for these operations and never expires; it is listed and revoked with the sessions.

client_capabilities._note: Device features a client may offer a document beyond rendering blocks. media.audio (the shared audio host, docs/media-audio.md) is what the play action needs, media.picker the pick action's; secure.screen, a window that can't be captured, is the Android app's (it applies it to every protected document); device.media-sync, the client's own background backup of the device's media to a media.sync provider (the Android app's), is what the sync action opens; the rest are reserved names no client claims yet. A document that requires one a client doesn't offer is shown as needing a newer app.
